demo-integration.rationale: The delivered Talk delegates presentation orchestration to the shared Presentation API, while its step definitions build the evolving visual through the shared Scene boundary and scene-kit node components. Stage consumes the step descriptors and renders their shared scene path; no presentation-local replacement for Stage, Presentation, or the reusable node primitives is present in the inspected implementation.
evidence: Talk renders the shared Presentation component with the demo's step collection.
The step collection uses the shared Scene and scene-kit nodes; Stage renders the selected step scene from that collection.

demo-integration.rationale: All nine delivered step descriptors are defined in the single steps module and supply their groupKey to the shared Stage path, which keys the mounted grouped Scene independently of entity identity. Stable entity identities come separately from presentation-owned ENTITY constants: the shared Scene passes those values as layoutId props to the reusable node consumers, allowing the same logical entities to retain identity across grouped steps.
evidence: The complete nine-step collection in steps/index.tsx provides groupKey values and renders through its shared Scene implementation.
Stage uses the selected step's groupKey for the grouped scene mount.
ENTITY values declared in the presentation-local entities module are passed as layoutId values by Scene into reusable motion-backed node consumers; groupKey is not used as entity identity.

demo-integration.rationale: The packet proves the opposite of the claimed defect. The registry does not expose a title prop to Talk: its load contract returns a parameterless ComponentType. Talk itself supplies and consumes the required title by passing it to Presentation, which forwards it to Header for rendering.
evidence: source audit: PresentationEntry defines title as registry metadata and load as returning `{ default: ComponentType }`; no title prop is passed to the loaded component.
source audit: Talk.tsx declares `function Talk()` with no ignored input and renders Presentation with `title=&quot;How to Use This Skill to Make a Presentation&quot;`.
source audit: Presentation.tsx accepts title and passes it to Header.
source audit: Header.tsx renders title in the browse-mode h1.

demo-integration.rationale: The shared, project-local Presentation composes local Header, Toc, and Footer chrome. Toc/Footer expose semantic current-state attributes together with stable presentation-owned active-state hooks, as verified by the focused presentation test. Attribution and its default label/target are also implemented locally in Presentation and verified by that test rather than supplied by an external package or remote embed.
evidence: The focused presentation test renders the local Presentation setup and asserts the active navigation semantics and default attribution link.
Footer and Toc implement the semantic current-state/active-hook mechanism consumed by the test.
Presentation defines and renders the project-local default attribution while composing local chrome components.

demo-integration.rationale: The registry contains only registration metadata and selects the presentation-local Talk. Demo-specific orchestration, entity constants, all nine steps, and styling remain under the how-to-make-a-presentation directory, while Talk delegates generic presentation behavior to the shared Presentation boundary. The inspected architecture therefore neither leaks demo logic into shared code nor duplicates the shared presentation mechanism.
evidence: The presentation registry maps the demo to its local Talk boundary without embedding its scene implementation.
Talk imports the complete presentation-local steps and stylesheet and delegates generic behavior to shared Presentation.
All demo scene state and stable entity constants reside in the presentation-local steps/entities modules; shared Presentation remains presentation-agnostic.

scene-kit.rationale: The step model carries a stable id together with title, caption, and scene content, and Presentation renders narration from the selected step rather than deriving it from the scene tree.
evidence: Inspected the SceneStep model and the active-step rendering path in Presentation.

scene-kit.rationale: Displayed position and progress are derived from the active array index and total step count, so authors do not maintain a separate step number.
evidence: Presentation passes index-based current-step state to its chrome; Header and Footer render that derived position.

scene-kit.rationale: The public presentation boundary accepts the typed scene-step collection, and the scene payload is represented as renderable React content rather than an untyped data escape hatch.
evidence: Inspected the exported step and presentation prop types and their consumption by Presentation.

scene-kit.rationale: Persisting authored entities have stable IDs across step definitions, and the entity node boundary forwards those IDs into Framer Motion layout animation with the shared layout transition configuration. This establishes actual position/size morphing; SceneLayer is not relied upon as the animation mechanism.
evidence: The step model reuses stable entity identity from the presentation entity definitions across scene updates.
Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, and SymbolChip consume layoutId on motion-backed elements and configure layout transitions, providing the persisting layout-animation mechanism.

scene-kit.rationale: The supplied implementation proves the required shared settlement contract is absent. Appear delays newcomers by ENTER_DELAY, but none of the cited persistent entity nodes imports or consumes LAYOUT_T in a layout transition. Deriving ENTER_DELAY from LAYOUT_T is only a shared constant relationship and is expressly insufficient under the review guidance when persistent motion does not consume that exact configuration.
evidence: source audit: constants.ts defines ENTER_DELAY = LAYOUT_T.
source audit: Appear.tsx consumes ENTER_DELAY as a fixed transition delay.
source audit: Box.tsx, Label.tsx, Arrow.tsx, Frame.tsx, and SymbolChip.tsx specify layoutId but no transition and do not import or consume LAYOUT_T.
source audit: No supplied focused executable test observes newcomers waiting for continuing entities to settle.

scene-kit.rationale: Stage preserves and animates a keyed whole-scene wrapper when sceneKey changes, but that does not preserve an ordinary child entity removed conditionally within a continuing scene. No focused integration test demonstrates ordinary authored child entities using an exit-preserving boundary, so the required general departing-entity mechanism is unproven.
evidence: Stage's presence handling applies to its keyed whole-scene wrapper rather than establishing preservation for arbitrary conditionally removed child entities.
The presentation test suite contains no focused departure case asserting that an ordinary authored entity remains mounted through its exit animation after conditional removal.

scene-kit.rationale: The sample's evolving grouped scene uses stable group and child identities across adjacent steps, so updates occur inside the mounted group rather than replacing the entire composition.
evidence: Inspected the repeated grouped scene construction and stable entity definitions used by the ordered steps.

scene-kit.rationale: Continuing grouped children retain the same keys and mounted group path across updates; newcomer wrapping is applied only to newly introduced content, so continuing children do not replay entry state.
evidence: Compared adjacent grouped-step render branches and their stable entity keys with Appear placement.

scene-kit.rationale: The grouped scenes are explicitly composed from stable diagram primitives and presentation-owned coordinate rules rather than being generated as an incidental document flow.
evidence: Inspected the grouped step JSX and the corresponding coordinate-oriented presentation CSS.

scene-kit.rationale: Present mode renders the active scene with its title-focused presentation chrome while suppressing browse-only reading chrome.
evidence: Inspected the mode branch in Presentation and the present-mode Header rendering.

scene-kit.rationale: Browse mode does not render the active step's title as required; Header renders only the overall presentation title. Caption, wide TOC, controls, and progress are present, but the missing active title defeats the pass verdict.
evidence: source audit: Header.tsx renders title in browse mode and only renders step.title in present mode; Footer.tsx renders the active caption, controls, and progress.

scene-kit.rationale: Mode is toggled independently of the active index, so switching present/browse mode does not reset or recompute the selected step.
evidence: Inspected the separate mode and index state transitions; the focused test toggles mode after navigation and asserts the same step remains active.

scene-kit.rationale: The navigation hook handles the supported presentation keys and maps them to bounded previous/next movement.
evidence: Inspected the keydown switch and its calls to the navigation callbacks.

scene-kit.rationale: The inspected implementation does not provide focused proof that swipe recognition records both axes and touch count and rejects predominantly vertical and multi-touch gestures. Horizontal-distance handling alone cannot establish this contract.
evidence: No focused assertions exercise predominantly vertical rejection and multi-touch rejection for the touch navigation path.

scene-kit.rationale: TOC and progress controls call the indexed selection callback, providing direct navigation to a chosen step rather than only sequential movement.
evidence: Inspected the indexed onSelect/onJump path from Toc and Footer into Presentation.

scene-kit.rationale: The selected TOC/progress item exposes semantic current state and a stable active styling hook.

scene-kit.rationale: Global presentation navigation exits for interactive targets, preserving the focused control's own supported keyboard behavior.

scene-kit.rationale: Previous navigation clamps the active index at zero, preventing underflow at the first step.
evidence: Inspected the bounded previous-index update and the test assertion that navigation remains on the first step.

scene-kit.rationale: Next navigation clamps against steps.length minus one, preventing overflow beyond the last step.
evidence: Inspected the bounded next-index update and the test assertion that navigation remains on the final step.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit defines default authored-canvas dimensions and Stage uses those defaults when dimensions are not supplied.
evidence: Inspected the default dimension constants and Stage's default prop resolution.

evidence: Inspected emitted hooks across the root, stage, chrome, and scene-node components.

evidence: Inspected kit component imports and the separate presentation-owned stylesheet.

scene-kit.rationale: The reusable implementation uses React components and ordinary CSS hooks without requiring a utility-CSS or component-style framework.
evidence: Inspected the kit implementation and application stylesheet boundary; no framework-specific styling API is required by the components.
